title: Spurs warn season ticket holders not to resell NBA Finals seats on unauthorized sites
content:
The San Antonio Spurs are warning season ticket holders trying to resell their NBA Finals seats on the secondary market not to sell them on unauthorized websites and have even revoked one fan’s season tickets.

One fan, Mark Burnett, posted a screenshot to Instagram of an email from another fan, warning Spurs fans to be careful about where they post their finals tickets for resale. In the email, the fan’s season-ticket membership was revoked immediately after the Spurs identified the ticket sales as originating from an unofficial secondary-market site that violates the ticketing terms and conditions.

“We’re focused on getting authentic tickets into the hands of our fans and strongly encourage fans to only buy from verified marketplaces,” the Spurs said in a statement to The Athletic. “Our resale guidelines have been communicated to our members throughout the season and in conjunction with Playoffs and Finals going on sale.”

The news comes amid soaring ticket prices as the NBA Finals tip off Wednesday at 8:30 p.m. at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio. The Spurs venue seats 18,418, and the venue’s third-party operator, Ticketmaster, is selling resale tickets. As of Tuesday, the cheapest ticket is $793.73 before fees in the balcony level in the 200s section. One of the best seats is on the floor in the Ledger Courtside Club and is marked $47,600 before fees. The Spurs will also host an official watch party for all finals games.

The Knicks are in the finals for the first time since 1999 and are hoping to win their first title in 53 years. The Spurs were last in the finals in 2014, when they beat the Miami Heat to earn their fifth title.

— Jared Weiss contributed to this story.
